question: After initial readiness, can a fresh private Shared Drive mount tolerate routine indexing intervals for one hour and then complete the first uncached read of the run-owned 85-byte file?
kind: Pre-registered correction to the instantaneous-ready liveness gate; read-only, one account and one exact run-owned file.
prior_result: google-shared-late-uncached-diagnostic-live.json failed after eight minutes only because the account summary was not ready; it did not retain the exact feed state. Cirrove sets a feed to indexing on every refresh and maps any non-ready feed to updating_or_offline.
arms: A: start the installed merged binary with fresh private account state, a private Shared Drive mount and btrfs-backed TMPDIR/SQLITE_TMPDIR; require an initial sample with account and all feeds ready

B: take 61 samples at 60-second intervals with no external traversal or content read; accept only feed states ready or indexing, require every last success younger than five minutes, and record safe feed-state names and numeric maximum age
C: fail immediately on sign_in_required, throttled, offline, rebuilding, unavailable, missing feeds, stale success, mount loss, save refusal, failed uploads or stuck changes
D: require an empty private content cache, read only the pre-registered run-owned file once through FUSE, and require its 85 bytes and private SHA-256
E: stop only the recorded private daemon PID and require its mount to disappear while the installed daemon PID and mount set remain unchanged
endpoint: Pass only if initial readiness holds, 61 samples span at least 3600 seconds with only ready/indexing feed states and fresh success, the cache is empty before the first content read, exact mounted bytes match, and cleanup preserves the installed baseline. Persist exact safe state enums and numeric age on failure, never account identifiers, tokens, URLs, cursors or provider bodies.
prediction: The prior two long arms likely sampled the expected indexing phase of a normal refresh. Allowing only that transient state should let the session reach the late read; any other state will instead identify a real liveness failure.
limits: One tiny file, one Workspace administrator and one Shared Drive. A pass does not establish large late downloads, restricted roles, 24-hour uptime, native document writeback or a memory trend.

startup_attempts_before_measurement.reason: control socket path exceeded the Unix-domain socket length limit
short socket parent was not a private mode-0700 directory

interpretation: The corrected liveness gate reached the registered endpoint. One sample caught the account summary as updating_or_offline while the only feed was the expected indexing state and its previous success was 31.588 seconds old; the remaining 60 samples were ready. This directly confirms that the prior instantaneous account-summary requirement could reject routine refresh work. After one hour with no content traversal, the private cache was empty and the first mounted read returned all 85 registered bytes with the expected SHA-256. The single run supports this exact read-only scenario only; its 1,912 KiB within-arm RSS spread is descriptive, not a memory-growth result.
next_probe: Use this refresh-tolerant feed-state gate for future controlled Shared Drive sessions. The remaining release evidence should target restricted Shared Drive roles, larger late downloads and native Google document behavior as separate pre-registered questions.
